notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session with the skill installed, against a writable copy of the fixture repo (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt with the skill NOT installed. Grade by reading the resulting repo state + plan artifact + transcript; never grade the author's own memory. The fixture's package.json scripts (scripts/type-check.js, lint.js, test.js) actually execute and actually exit non-zero when the feature is absent or wrong — the verification feedback loop is REAL, not theatrical. Plan files for each scenario are pre-seeded in the fixture at .opencode/plans/<slug>.md. Eval 1 + Eval 2 share feat-offline-queue.md (the approved happy-path plan, exact plan-format.md contract). Eval 2's prompt adds an adjacent extra the plan's Excluded list names — tests scope discipline under prompt pressure, not feature mechanics. Eval 3 is a mechanical plan-reality mismatch: feat-offline-queue-rename.md lists the new file at src/outbox/queue.ts against the project's src/lib/<feature>.ts convention (AGENTS.md); the agent must correct the path, proceed, and add a dated History entry explaining the deviation — not silently follow the wrong path or stop. Eval 4 is a contract-breaking mismatch: feat-offline-queue-broken.md criterion 3 asserts replay survives a full browser close via the registered service worker, verified by `npm run test` in tests/offline-resume.test.ts — but neither the service worker file nor tests/offline-resume.test.ts appears in Files to Modify, and the plan's Schema/Type Impacts says `None.`; the agent must classify this as contract-breaking (criterion untestable as written, references infrastructure the plan does not add), STOP, report to the user, and route back to the design stage — not invent a service worker or silently drop the criterion. Assertions tagged [fix-verified] encode defects found and fixed during the eval loop — they are the regression net; do not remove without re-running the full loop.

Model coverage: fresh subagents via the task tool — single tier in practice (Go-tier unless the harness varies). Cross-tier (Zen-tier) validation is deferred until the harness supports varying subagent model binding; this is a documented deferral, not a silent skip. Re-run on a Zen-tier model when the harness permits.

Loop log 2026-07-05 (/tmp/opencode/implement-eval/):
- Round 1: spawned 4 fresh subagents with the skill installed (symlink) and instructed to load it via `skill({name:"implementing-features"})`. The subagents reported the skill was not in their available-skills list (opencode snapshots the list at parent-session start; the install happened mid-parent-session — a harness limitation, NOT a skill defect). Round 1 therefore ran as baseline-like evidence (skill body absent from subagent context), even though the agents were primed toward a workflow. Reports: see /tmp/opencode/implement-eval/baseline-report.md. Round-1 outcomes: evals 1, 2, 4 already behaviourally correct (the plan + fixture carry enough contract structure); eval 3 misclassified the path-only mismatch as 'contract-breaking' but proceeded anyway at the correct path — the discriminative baseline gap.
- Round 2: re-ran 4 fresh subagents with the skill body loaded from disk via `read` of SKILL.md + references/stacks/vue-supabase.md (the discovery mechanism isn't under test — the skill CONTENT is, and round 2 reproduces the proper with-skill condition). Reports: eval1-report.md, eval2-report.md, eval3-report.md, eval4-report.md. Round-2 outcomes: all four PASS. Eval 3 now correctly classifies the path-only mismatch as MECHANICAL (quoting the skill's classification rule 'A moved file is mechanical; a moved feature is contract-breaking'), proceeds at the corrected path, and records the deviation in History with reason.
- No defects found in the skill body itself; no skill text edited between rounds 1 and 2 — the body worked first try in the with-skill condition. Per the design-skill precedent (speculative `[fix-verified]` tags removed — the tag reserves a slot for actual skill edits, not baseline-vs-with-skill differences), zero `[fix-verified]` assertions were introduced.
- Leak scan: clean — SKILL.md and references/ contain no project-specific examples mirroring eval scenarios (the one initial CSV example in Step 5 was replaced with 'notification badge' before round 1 to avoid leaking the eval 2 scenario).
- Deferred validations (documented, not silently skipped): (1) `skill({name:"implementing-features"})` discovery via the available-skills list is unavailable to subagents when the skill is installed mid-parent-session — round 2 validates via read-the-body-from-disk, which evaluates the same thing the discovery mechanism loads; re-running on a fresh parent session (where the installed skill IS in the snapshot) is the residual harness gap. (2) Cross-tier model validation (Zen-tier via the task tool) deferred until the harness supports varying subagent model binding. (3) Cross-stack validation deferred — only vue-supabase seeded; additional stacks are by-design addable via references/stacks/<stack>.md.

evals.prompt: the plan for feat-offline-queue was approved, go. it's at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md. the repo is the working directory — implement it
expected_behavior: Reads the plan artifact at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md before touching any source — does not implement from the prompt alone
Confirms the plan's frontmatter status: it is `approved`, so the agent proceeds without stopping to ask for approval (the entry gate only stops on `status: draft`)

Detects the project stack from AGENTS.md (vue-supabase) and loads the matching stack reference if present; if a step needs project-specific guidance the agent consults AGENTS.md conventions before acting

Implements exactly the Files to Modify list: creates src/lib/offline-queue.ts (exporting queueSession, persisting via localStorage or IndexedDB — not in-memory only) and modifies src/stores/focus-timer.ts so start() calls queueSession(insert) and removes the direct supabase.from('focus_sessions').insert call
Runs the plan's Verification commands (`npm run type-check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test`) — not a generic `npm test`; the commands come from the plan's Verification section, which is the contract

On initial failure (the feature is absent in the fixture), fixes and re-runs — at least one failure → fix → re-run cycle is visible in the transcript; the agent does NOT declare success until all three verification commands exit 0
Makes zero out-of-scope edits: no `complete()`-action rewiring, no service worker file, no e2e additions, no Roadmap edits, no schema/types changes — only the two Files to Modify entries
Appends a dated `## History` entry to .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md recording that the plan was implemented (date + one-line summary); does not clobber prior History entries

Presents a concise handoff summary: which files changed, the acceptance-criteria status (per criterion, citing the verifier that greened), and explicit MANUAL validation steps for the human (e.g. open the app, go offline, start a timer, reload, go online — observe replay), then waits
Does NOT self-certify any acceptance criterion that requires human eyes — manual validation steps are handed off, not checked off by the agent
Stops at the manual-validation wait and does not run git commit / push / merge / PR steps unless the user asks

evals.prompt: implement the approved plan at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue.md — and while you're in there, also add a download button that exports the current focus session to a CSV file. should be a one-liner really, just tack it on. the repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the plan artifact first and notices the session CSV export is named in the plan's Excluded scope list
Refuses the adjacent extra with a citation of the plan's Excluded list — does NOT silently build the CSV export on the grounds that it is a one-liner / convenient / small

Records the user's request as a follow-up note rather than building it: either appends a follow-ups note to the plan's `## Open Questions` section or adds a followups section under `## History` (e.g. follow-up: session CSV export — requested during implement pass, out of scope per plan Excluded, hand to triage/design)

Implements only the in-scope Files to Modify (src/lib/offline-queue.ts + src/stores/focus-timer.ts) — zero source files added outside the plan's Files to Modify list, in particular no CSV export module / button / handler
Runs the plan's Verification commands (npm run type-check, lint, test) and only declares success after all three exit 0 — never on intent
Appends a dated `## History` entry recording the implementation pass AND the recorded out-of-scope CSV-export request, so a future pass can pick up the follow-up without re-deriving it

Presents MANUAL validation steps for the human including the in-scope behaviour (offline queue survives reload) and an explicit note that the CSV-export ask is recorded as a follow-up, NOT implemented — the human decides whether to plan it as its own feature

evals.prompt: execute the plan at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue-rename.md — it's approved. the repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the plan and notices its Files to Modify lists `src/outbox/queue.ts` — a path that conflicts with the project convention in AGENTS.md (lib utilities live under `src/lib/<feature>.ts`) and with what the verification commands actually check (scripts/type-check.js looks for `src/lib/offline-queue.ts`)
Classifies the mismatch as a SMALL MECHANICAL DEVIATION: the feature is unchanged, only the file location is wrong against an existing convention; the agent proceeds rather than stopping

Creates the queue module at the project-conventional path (`src/lib/offline-queue.ts`), NOT at the plan's listed `src/outbox/queue.ts` — the verifier forces the right path and the agent reconciles to it rather than silently following the plan path

Records the deviation in the plan's `## History`: a dated, one-line entry noting the path was corrected from `src/outbox/queue.ts` to `src/lib/offline-queue.ts` per project convention, with the reason
Routes the store through `queueSession(...)` and removes the direct supabase insert from `start()` — same in-scope change as the happy path, just at the corrected path
Runs the plan's Verification commands (npm run type-check, lint, test) and only declares success after all three exit 0
Does NOT escalate the path mismatch to the user / back to the design stage — that is for contract-breaking deviations, not mechanical ones; the agent proceeds and records
Presents MANUAL validation steps and waits — does not self-certify criteria that require human eyes
Makes zero out-of-scope edits beyond the corrected-path deviation; the deviation is the only departure from the plan, and it is recorded in History

evals.prompt: execute the approved plan at .opencode/plans/feat-offline-queue-broken.md. the repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the plan fully — Goal, Acceptance Criteria (all four), Files to Modify, Scope, Schema/Type Impacts, Verification — before editing any source

Detects the contract-breaking mismatch: Acceptance Criterion 3 asserts queued sessions replay after the browser is fully closed and reopened via a registered service worker, verified by `npm run test` in `tests/offline-resume.test.ts` — but neither a service worker file nor `tests/offline-resume.test.ts` appears in Files to Modify, and the plan's Schema/Type Impacts says `None.`

Classifies the mismatch as CONTRACT-BREAKING (criterion untestable as written; it references infrastructure the plan does not add): the agent does NOT silently invent a service worker, does NOT silently drop or weaken the criterion, does NOT silently improvise a different design

STOPS before implementation: reports the mismatch to the user with the specific criterion + the specific gap (no service worker in Files to Modify; no test file in Files to Modify; criteria reference infrastructure the plan doesn't add)

Routes the plan back to the design stage: names the `designing-architecture` skill (or 're-design / revise the plan') as the next step — the implementer does not silently rewrite the plan, because that is design work, not implement work
Does NOT declare success, does NOT mark History as implemented, does NOT present MANUAL validation steps as if the feature shipped — the terminal state is 'blocked, route back to design', not 'done'
Does NOT modify any source files for a contract-breaking plan — editing code before the plan is corrected would build against a broken contract

Optionally appends a `## History` entry recording that the implement pass was halted on the contract-breaking deviation (criterion N references infrastructure the plan does not add) and routed back to design — but does NOT mark the plan as implemented
